## Description {#details}

Reflection utilities for the µTest++ testing framework.

The <code>reflection</code> namespace provides facilities for obtaining source location information and type names at compile time, thereby supporting advanced reporting and diagnostics within the µTest++ framework.

It includes a local implementation of <code><a href="/micro-test-plus-xpack/docs/api/classes/micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus/reflection/source-location">source&#95;location</a></code> for environments lacking C++20 standard support, as well as utilities for extracting concise type names from compiler-specific macros such as <code>&#95;&#95;PRETTY&#95;FUNCTION&#95;&#95;</code>.

All definitions within this namespace are intended to facilitate advanced reflection and reporting capabilities.

### short&#95;name() {#ab4fa1159ebe60ce5fe073eefbe9a2446}

<MemberDefinition
  prototype={<>const char &#42; micro&#95;os&#95;plus::micro&#95;test&#95;plus::reflection::short&#95;name (const char &#42; name)</>}>
Extract a short type or function name from a fully qualified name.

<ParametersList title="Parameters">
<ParametersListItem name="name">The fully qualified name as a C-string.</ParametersListItem>
</ParametersList>

<SectionUser title="Returns">
A pointer to the short name within the input string.
</SectionUser>

This function extracts the short name from a given file path by locating the final folder separator (&#39;/&#39;). If a separator is found, it returns a pointer to the character immediately following it, effectively providing the file or folder name. If no separator is present, the original input string is returned. This utility is useful for reporting concise file or folder names in test output.

### type&#95;name() {#a6580ad54ad22a1d3ab43a1d9d49d1f26}

<MemberDefinition

Extract the type name from the <code>&#95;&#95;PRETTY&#95;FUNCTION&#95;&#95;</code> macro.

This function template parses the compiler-specific <code>&#95;&#95;PRETTY&#95;FUNCTION&#95;&#95;</code> macro to extract a concise type name for the template parameter <code>T</code>.

The implementation is compiler-dependent and may require adjustment for different toolchains. It is primarily intended for internal use within the µTest++ framework to support improved diagnostics and reporting.
